# Fenced 
::: {#id .class1 key=value}
This is a fenced div with an id, class, and key-value pair. You can use this to create custom containers in your Quarto documents.
:::

## 1. Applying Custom Backgrounds and Borders
You can combine standard CSS classes or your own styles.css properties. Here, we create a custom alert box:

::: {.bg-light .border .rounded .p-3}
### 💡 Quick Notice
This box has a light grey background, rounded corners, and padding. You can use standard Bootstrap utility classes directly inside Quarto!
:::

## 2. Creating Layout Columns (Side-by-Side Content)
Quarto recognizes the .columns and .column classes out of the box. This lets you put text, lists, or media next to each other easily:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="30%"}
### Left Column 30%
- **Item A:** A detailed point on the left side.
- **Item B:** Another piece of data.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Right Column 50%
Here is a paragraph explaining the context of the list on the left, keeping your page clean and highly readable.
:::
:::

## 3. Styling Bullet Lists or Tables
If you want to apply a style to an entire block—like your lists or tables—without adding classes to every single line, wrap them in a fenced div:

::: {.text-muted .small}
- This list is formatted with smaller, muted text.
- It is excellent for footnotes, disclaimers, or minor references.
- All elements inside inherit these text rules.
:::


##  4. Nesting Fenced Divs
If you want to place a fenced div inside another one, simply increase the number of colons for the outer block so Quarto knows where it starts and ends:markdown:::: {.border .p-4}
This is the outer container block.

:::: {.border .p-5}
This is the outer container block.

::: {.text-success}
  This is an inner block with green text.
:::

::::

# Callouts

## 1. Standard Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
### Note
This is a standard note callout. Use this for general, neutral information you want readers to notice.
:::

## 2. Custom Callouts - Tip
::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
This is a tip callout. Great for shortcuts, helpful hints, or best practices.
:::

## 3. Custom Callouts - Important

::: {.callout-important}
### Important
This is an important callout. Use this for critical details that shouldn't be missed.
:::

## 4. Custom Callouts - Warning and Caution
::: {.callout-warning}
### Warning
This is a warning callout. Ideal for alerting users about potential errors or unexpected outcomes.
:::

## 5. Custom Callouts - Caution
::: {.callout-caution}
### Caution
This is a caution callout. Typically used to advise users about dangerous steps or data loss.
:::


## 6. Custom Callouts - Success
::: {.callout-success}
### Success
This is a success callout. Use this to highlight positive results, achievements, or successful operations
:::


## 7. Custom Callouts - Question
::: {.callout-question}
### Question
This is a question callout. Perfect for prompting users to think, reflect, or consider alternatives
:::


# Advanced Callouts 
You can control how callout blocks behave and look by adding specific attributes inside the curly braces {}.

## 1. Collapsible Callouts
If you have a long explanation or solution that you want to hide by default, make it collapsible using collapse="true":

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
### 🔍 Click to reveal the Solution

To fix the rendering issue, make sure your `.css` filename matches exactly what is specified inside your document's YAML header.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
### 🔍 Click to reveal the Toogle Solution
This is false setting
To fix the rendering issue, make sure your `.css` filename matches exactly what is specified inside your document's YAML header.
:::


## 2. Clean Look (Removing Icons)
If you want the color-coded box but prefer a cleaner look without the default icon, use icon="false":

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
### Minimalist Callout
This box uses the note styling but completely hides the icon graphic for a cleaner visual layout.
:::


## 3. Minimal Styling (Border Only)
Quarto has built-in layout styles for callouts. You can change appearance="minimal" to get a clean left-border line instead of a fully filled background block:

::: {.callout-warning appearance="minimal"}
### Heads Up!
This callout uses the minimal look. It has a colored left border with no background fills.
:::
